source: Yet the shift has recently stabilized, and it could even reverse.
claim: Among non-animated films with a known medium, the digital-only share rose from 74.5% in 2014 to 83.0% in 2016, then dipped slightly to 82.4% in 2017.

source: Between 2015 and 2017, only 4% of sci-fi movies were shot purely in film, lower than the rate among all genres (11% of movies were still shot purely in film).
claim: Among non-animated 2015-2017 films with a known medium, 3.6% of sci-fi films were shot on film only, against 11.2% of all films.

source: Compared to the average across all genres, sci-fi movies are more likely to be shot using digital cameras, either as the only medium or in tandem with film cameras.
claim: In 2015-2017, 96.4% of non-animated sci-fi films with a known medium used digital (digital only or both), against 88.8% of all such films.

source: Horror is another genre with a high digital adoption rate. But unlike science fiction, the dominance of digital has occurred in more recent years.
claim: The digital share of horror films (digital only or both) was 21.2% in 2006-2008, 29.6% in 2009-2011, 75.0% in 2012-2014 and 100.0% in 2015-2017, while sci-fi's had already reached 52.3% in 2009-2011.

source: Between 2015 and 2017, 17% of drama movies were still shot on film.
claim: Among non-animated 2015-2017 films with a known medium, 17.0% of drama films were shot on film only.

source: Movies with lower budget ranges ($20M or less) are more likely to use digital than movies in higher budget ranges—perhaps the digital camera is a more appealing budget choice after all.
claim: The digital-only share was highest in the under-$20M range in every period: 13.3% in 2006-2008, 24.3% in 2009-2011, 74.6% in 2012-2014 and 92.3% in 2015-2017.

source: Interestingly, budget limits are more apparent for movies shot using both film and digital, where its most common in the highest budget range (more than $160M).
claim: In 2015-2017, 23.5% of non-animated films budgeted over $160M with a known medium were shot on both film and digital, against 1.9%, 6.5%, 2.2% and 7.1% in the lower budget ranges.

source: Between 2015-2017, 6% of movies in lower budget ranges still shot on film, similar in proportion to movies in the highest budget range.
claim: In 2015-2017, 5.8% of non-animated films budgeted under $20M with a known medium were shot on film only, close to 5.9% of films over $160M.

source: Beside big budget movies such as Star Wars: Force Awakens (2015) and Dunkirk (2017), lower budget movies such as Gifted (2017) and The Beguiled (2017) still manage to shoot on film in the last three years.
claim: Among 2015-2017 films shot on film are Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens (2015, $306M), Dunkirk (2017, $150M), Gifted (2017, $7M) and The Beguiled (2017, $10.5M).

source: A decade ago, the majority of directors still chose to shoot on film, but around 2012 more directors began to prefer digital.
claim: Among directors with at least one known-format film in a period, 74.0% in 2006-2008 shot only on film, while in 2012-2014 62.4% shot only digitally and 23.6% only on film.

source: Christopher Nolan shot all of his movies on film, including his latest movie Dunkirk (2017).
claim: All of Christopher Nolan's films in the data, from The Prestige (2006) to Dunkirk (2017), are recorded with film as the medium.

source: Quentin Tarantino is another example of a film loyalist; he even states that he would stop making movies if he cannot shoot on film anymore.
claim: All of Quentin Tarantino's films in the data, from Death Proof (2007) to The Hateful Eight (2015), are recorded with film as the medium.

source: On the other side, we also have early adopters who jumped to digital in 2006-2008 and have been using it ever since, such as Robert Rodriguez. He started to shoot on digital in 2002 with Spy Kids 2 and shot all of his later films in the same medium.
claim: Every Robert Rodriguez film in the data with a known medium (2007-2014) is recorded as digital, while three titles have an unknown medium.

source: Judd Apatow returned to film on his latest movie Trainwreck (2015) after previously using digital on This is 40 (2012).
claim: Judd Apatow's This Is 40 (2012) is recorded as digital and his later Trainwreck (2015) as film.

source: Some directors such as Danny Boyle use both technologies. In Steve Jobs (2015), he used both digital and film formats to cover Apple’s product launch on different timelines.
claim: Danny Boyle's Steve Jobs (2015) is recorded as shot on both film and digital.

source: As a cinematographer who has worked with both film and digital camera, Rodrigo Prieto has his own reason to choose digital for Passengers
claim: Passengers (2016) is recorded as shot on digital.

source: While in Silence, he used both medium but had different use cases for each one
